chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who was fierce upon his wife, or a woman who was fierce upon her husband, so one of them killed the other. He said: There is nothing upon both of them if they are trustworthy. So if they are suspected, they are required to swear an oath by Allah that they did not intend the killing.

key_terms.أَعْنَفَ: To be fierce or prone to anger

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a husband and wife kill each other in a fit of anger?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'al-afwan' (exemption from blood money) in cases of mutual homicide arising from sudden, uncontrolled rage, provided the parties are deemed trustworthy and not habitual aggressors. The requirement of an oath (yamin) upon suspicion underscores the evidentiary burden placed on proving intent, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving life and avoiding punitive financial liability in ambiguous domestic conflicts.
